note: Most widely-documented roller figures (CEMA/ISO) come from bulk-material handling and do NOT transfer to unit/tote/carton handling -- these duty classes are unit-handling specific, each sourced from a real catalog rather than a bulk-conveyor chart.

light.note: Small/light carton roller track, tight pitch.

standard.source: Hytrol 1.9in gravity roller conveyor -- the de facto NA industry-standard bed for cartons/totes, 5-75 lb duty
standard.note: Most common gravity/idle roller bed for cartons and totes.

mdr.source: Interroll RollerDrive EC5000 datasheet (50mm cylindrical, IP54); idle/slave roller pitch assumed to match standard duty class
mdr.note: 24V motor-driven-roller zone: one drive roller + 2-4 idle/slave rollers per zone, linked by O-ring bands.

min_rollers_under_item_rule_of_thumb.note: Widely cited industry rule of thumb (at least 3 rollers under the smallest item at all times). NOT confirmed against a specific manufacturer catalog page during this research pass -- treat as a design heuristic to drive default pitch selection, not as a sourced spec.

belt_pulley_diameter_estimate.note: Interpolated estimate for tote/carton-scale belt conveyors. Manufacturer data found only at bench-conveyor scale (25-32mm, e.g. MISUMI flat belt conveyors) and CEMA bulk scale (200mm+, ANSI/CEMA 402) -- this tool's scale sits in the documented gap between the two. Revisit if a real unit-handling belt catalog turns up a direct figure.
